comments.author: hateborne
comments.body:
Astra or Fable are god damned massively overkill for this. You're using a Lambo to get groceries. 

I use Fable at work when I'm working through changes both upstream and downstream of a service I support. This includes adding features to ABC service, preparing dependent services 123 & DEF, and expanding functionality to receive the new data from the outbound calls. This is across services written in four programming languages. Additionally, these changes are always pre flight checked by digging into AWS Cloudwatch and Splunk logging to verify the direction and path taken is correct, data backed, and safe to roll back (if needed).

You would fine using something like Sol 6.2 for most tasks, especially forcing that as your sub agent model, then Sol 5.6 for the larger tasks that require complex, multi step reasoning. If you're providing clear, well articulated instructions: you can likely just ride out Sol 6.2 for everything. 

Disclaimer: I'm exclusively a Claude user at home and Cursor (using Claude and Cursor models) at work. My knowledge of ChatGPT-land is surface level
